questions.text: How does Korean palace architecture differ from Chinese imperial palaces in terms of climate adaptation, site integration, and heating strategy?

Chinese palaces emphasize axial cosmic geometry and glazed tiles; Korean palaces adapt topography, integrate ondol heating, and use restrained decoration emphasizing site responsiveness.
Korean palaces are smaller copies of Chinese models without innovation, lacking distinct architectural identity
Korean palaces emphasize elaborate ornamental display; Chinese palaces use minimalist design, which is contrary to historical evidence

rationale.a: The article clearly establishes distinct architectural strategies in Korean versus Chinese imperial design.
rationale.c: Korean architecture represents adaptive synthesis and innovation, not mere copying.
rationale.d: Both Chinese and Korean emphasize refined craft; Korean uses restraint as cultivated sophistication.
rationale.correct: The article explicitly contrasts Chinese (axial cosmic geometry, glazed tiles) with Korean (topography adaptation, ondol heating, restrained decoration, cultivated craft). Korean architecture prioritizes site responsiveness and thermal comfort.
rationale.takeaway: Korean architecture prioritizes site responsiveness and thermal comfort.
